topics.topic: Atomic acquisition and rollback across multiple listener bindings
questions: If concurrent starts split a set of listener bindings between them, must acquisition be all-or-nothing, and must every partially acquired listener be released immediately when the start cannot acquire the rest?
When several listeners are configured, must acquisition be all-or-nothing, and what happens to listeners already bound if a later binding fails?

quotes:
The checks run in one
   order and the first that fails stops the start: the service tokens and the
   service API's address all five or none — none makes an owner-only start,
   and some but not all fail on the first missing one in rule 1's order; every other item of rule 1 present; each well formed; the two addresses'
   ports different; each secret's length (rule 3);
   their distinctness (rule 4); the store and backup location apart (rule
   5); the backup location writable, by a probe file under the temporary
   prefix (A18 rule 5); the store opening, or made new (rule 5); last, the
   listener of each surface opened at its configured address (rule 1) — the
   owner interface's first, then the
   service API's unless the start is owner-only, one that cannot be opened
   failing the start and closing the one already opened.
judgement.why: A17 fixes sequential listener acquisition in one order and requires an already-opened listener to be closed when a later opening fails.

topics.topic: Required tests for A17 startup and listener concurrency guarantees
questions: What test must demonstrate the newly claimed concurrency behaviour for A17, including simultaneous starts, no serving before readiness, exclusive binding, and cleanup after partial acquisition failure?
Which A17 Required tests demonstrate the startup and exclusive-listener concurrency guarantee, and what exactly must those tests show?

quotes:
5. A start whose store is made new and whose listener then cannot be opened
   stops, serves nothing and removes that store — or, when the removal
   fails, leaves it as an empty store of the release's version; one whose
   listener cannot be opened over an existing store leaves that store's
   records as they were. An owner-only start opens no service API listener.

9. `[fe80::1%eth0]:8781`, `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]:8781`, `127.0.0.01:8781` and
   `127.0.0.1:08781` each stop the start, naming the item. While Registry
   runs, a second socket binding the service API's endpoint fails; an IPv4
   client cannot reach an IPv6 listener.
judgement.why: A17's Required tests state that listener-opening failure stops the start without serving and that a second binding of an active endpoint fails; the normative listener order and cleanup are already fixed by A17 rule 2.

topics.topic: Timing of listener binding relative to other startup checks
questions: When are listeners bound relative to the other startup checks: before them but kept non-serving, or only after every other check has passed?
Are listener bindings themselves checks that must all be acquired before the start is considered passed, or are all other checks completed first and listeners bound afterward?

quotes:
Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
   every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that
   names the failed item and never its value (R0-37).

the store opening, or made new (rule 5); last, the
   listener of each surface opened at its configured address (rule 1) — the
   owner interface's first, then the
   service API's unless the start is owner-only, one that cannot be opened
   failing the start and closing the one already opened.
judgement.why: A17 says listener opening is the last startup check, after the store is opened or made, and serving begins only after every check passes.

topics.topic: Complete normative A17 startup concurrency rules
questions: What are A17's actual normative rules for check order, listener-binding order, atomicity across multiple listeners, failure rollback, and the exact condition under which startup is refused?

quotes:
Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
   every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that
   names the failed item and never its value (R0-37). The checks run in one
   order and the first that fails stops the start: the service tokens and the
   service API's address all five or none — none makes an owner-only start,
   and some but not all fail on the first missing one in rule 1's order; every other item of rule 1 present; each well formed; the two addresses'
   ports different; each secret's length (rule 3);
   their distinctness (rule 4); the store and backup location apart (rule
   5); the backup location writable, by a probe file under the temporary
   prefix (A18 rule 5); the store opening, or made new (rule 5); last, the
   listener of each surface opened at its configured address (rule 1) — the
   owner interface's first, then the
   service API's unless the start is owner-only, one that cannot be opened
   failing the start and closing the one already opened. Within one
   check, items go in the order rule 1 lists them.
judgement.why: A17 expressly fixes the check order, listener order, refusal at the first failure, rollback of an earlier listener, and the prohibition on serving before all checks pass.

topics.topic: Exact network resource covered by exclusive listener ownership
questions: What exact resource must be exclusive: the textual configured address, the resolved socket endpoint, every address produced by name resolution, or the effective network endpoint including IPv4/IPv6 overlap and socket reuse options?

quotes:
Registry binds each listener
   exclusively — it sets no option that lets a second active socket bind
   an overlapping endpoint — and an IPv6 listener accepts IPv6 connections
   alone, never IPv4 ones mapped onto it; whether a port a closed listener
   left can be bound again at once is the platform's, which Registry
   neither requires nor prevents.

The two
   addresses have different ports, so that the two surfaces' endpoints
   never overlap, whatever their hosts.
judgement.why: A17 defines exclusivity in terms of overlapping active socket endpoints and explicitly excludes IPv4-mapped traffic from IPv6 listeners.

topics.topic: Missing accepted A17 decision required by the A21 reference
questions: How can A17 satisfy the Required-tests demand that every reference be an accepted decision of States 0–2 that exists in this text when no Accepted decision A17 is supplied?

quotes: ## Accepted decision A17 — configuration and secrets are checked before Registry serves

The configuration is a set of environment variables whose names begin
   with `REGISTRY_`, set as R0-23 says.
judgement.why: The full State 2 text contains Accepted decision A17, so A21's reference names an existing accepted decision.

topics.topic: Startup checks, refusal conditions, and owner-only fallback policy
questions: Which checks are included, which failures refuse the whole start, and which failures instead permit an owner-only start?

quotes:
The checks run in one
   order and the first that fails stops the start: the service tokens and the
   service API's address all five or none — none makes an owner-only start,
   and some but not all fail on the first missing one in rule 1's order; every other item of rule 1 present; each well formed; the two addresses'
   ports different; each secret's length (rule 3);
   their distinctness (rule 4); the store and backup location apart (rule
   5); the backup location writable, by a probe file under the temporary
   prefix (A18 rule 5); the store opening, or made new (rule 5); last, the
   listener of each surface opened at its configured address (rule 1) — the
   owner interface's first, then the
   service API's unless the start is owner-only, one that cannot be opened
   failing the start and closing the one already opened.

one service token
   for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel
   (R0-20, R0-23) — and the address the service API listens on, or, for an
   owner-only start, none of these five: Registry then serves the owner
   interface alone,
   opening no listener of the service API, so a service call reaches no
   Registry and is refused by its connection failing, with no answer (owner,
   2026-11-01; A18 rule 9).
judgement.why: A17 enumerates every startup check and makes the all-five-or-none service configuration the sole owner-only exception; other failed checks stop startup.
